body: Locking protocol: every append takes a BLOCKING SHARED lock on .annot/.lock; compaction takes EXCLUSIVE with bounded try-lock retries. The spec originally mandated lockless appends, but a lockless append landing between compaction's read and its atomic rename writes to a replaced inode and is silently lost — the two spec requirements were contradictory, and shared-lock appends were the user-approved resolution (one syscall per append; blocks only while a compaction holds the lock). fs4 calls must stay fully qualified (FileExt::lock_shared) because std::fs::File grew inherent lock methods in Rust 1.89 that shadow the trait with a different TryLockError type.
